notes: §1989:A.2.30.4 RV2: "The number of digits returned is 18." Read with §1989:A.2.30.3 AR3 ("The total number of digits in argument-1 must not exceed 18."), the duty at 85 is a returned value that carries all 18 digits of a conforming argument, at any scale. RenderDec routes NUMVAL-C to NumvalCDec in every arithmetic mode and channel (ReturnsExactParse, no edition arm); NvScan counts digits only, skipping the currency string and the grouping commas, accumulates them in an Int128, and NumvalCDec lifts the result to the 34-digit decimal carrier exactly at the parsed scale. Probed at --std 85: 18 digits as a grouped integer, as 9.9 after a currency sign and as V18, in COMPUTE and in a relation, each exact to the last digit. The witness converts 18 digits in six comma groups after a currency sign.

next.reason: 1985 fixes the size of the NUMVAL-C result: 'The number of digits returned is 18.' No 2023 rule fixes a returned digit count. §2023:15.68.4 RV1 ('The returned value is the numeric value represented by argument-1') restates 1985 RV1, and §2023:15.68.3 AR6/AR7 restate 1985 AR3's limit on argument-1 digits (31/35/34), so neither states this requirement. Instead §2023:15.4.1 says 'When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor.' That paragraph has no catalog id. The fixed 18-digit size is therefore dropped. A conforming 1985 argument has at most 18 digits, so its value is the same.
